system: You are a qualitative researcher doing open coding of public feedback about SIPs. You never recommend funds or stocks. Quotes must be copied character-for-character. Output JSON only.
prompt:
Open-code this tradingqna text. Research questions:
  start     - Why did the person start a SIP, and what did they expect to happen?
  behaviour - What changed in their behaviour in the months after starting (checking returns, increasing,
              reducing, skipping, redeeming, switching, sticking with it, feelings about it)?
  stop      - What led them (or investors they describe) to pause, reduce or stop a SIP, or nearly do so?

Write short free-text codes (2-8 words, your own words) for every distinct idea the text supports. Several
codes per question are fine; skip questions the text says nothing about. Each code needs a verbatim quote
(an exact substring of the text; shorten it but never reword or translate).

Return: {"record_id": "tradingqna_df429ff00b23", "codes": [{"question": "start"|"behaviour"|"stop", "code": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

CONTEXT (video/topic title, background only): New SIPs are down to March 2017 levels while old SIP cancellations are making new highs. What does this mean for the markets?
TEXT:
<<<
Most SIP investors set it up & forget. This helps AMCs, advisors etc to pocket regular money. Some investors who monitor their portfolio panic in such continuous market fall & stop SIPs…this is a regular phenomena. All ads on MF sahi hai etc have built the euphoria during market peaks & many are sitting on losses. As investors you need to understand the market dynamics & invest in quality stocks/index funds during such oversold territories, then book regular profits. This is the only mechanism which can deliver decent returns. I see that many who had invested in smallcase & other fancy products are all in shock as we see that more than 250 stocks have hit a new 52 week low on NSE (latest news).
>>>
